narrativeReportMd:
# ClinicalImpression R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`ClinicalImpression` appears to be removed from the supplied R6 ballot core package, with no direct renamed resource or single replacement StructureDefinition found. This is a hard R4-to-R6 instance break: a resource whose `resourceType` is `ClinicalImpression` can be valid in R4 but has no native R6 core resource definition.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 `StructureDefinition-ClinicalImpression.json` with the supplied R6 package. Because the expected R6 StructureDefinition is absent, the analysis searched the R6 package index and package contents for `ClinicalImpression`, `clinicalimpression`, and likely clinical-assessment counterparts. Base `Resource`/`DomainResource` and datatype changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
The dominant issue is artifact removal, not a per-element cardinality or type change. R4 data that used `status`, `subject`, `effective[x]`, `problem`, `investigation`, `finding`, `prognosis[x]`, and `supportingInfo` must be transformed to other R6 resources or retained through extensions/profiles. No local R6 resource was found that preserves the same aggregate clinical-assessment shape.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is the absence of the resource itself. A strict R6 validator, generated model, schema, API endpoint, or enum of resource types will not recognize `ClinicalImpression` instances. A second high-impact migration risk is that decomposition across `Condition`, `Observation`, `DiagnosticReport`, `RiskAssessment`, `CarePlan`, or other resources is profile-specific and not automatically lossless.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed to confirm the standards rationale and the intended migration strategy, because the local package did not include an official diff, ballot narrative, JIRA issue, or ConceptMap for this removal.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A less disruptive design could have kept `ClinicalImpression` in R6 as deprecated/retired, or provided a normative cross-version extension and ConceptMap. That would preserve wire compatibility while still steering implementers toward more specific resources.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the base-resource reports separately for inherited changes, and review related resource reports plus any official migration guidance before defining production transforms.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ClinicalImpression` is present in R4 but absent from the supplied R6 core package, producing a hard R4-to-R6 break for existing instances and generated APIs. The main migration concerns are resource-type rejection, loss of a single aggregate assessment container, and profile-specific mapping to other R6 resources. The top uncertainty is the absence of official rationale or a sanctioned ConceptMap.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is not a simple rename. Implementers should inventory R4 `ClinicalImpression` use, decide whether each record should become one or more `Condition`, `Observation`, `DiagnosticReport`, `RiskAssessment`, `CarePlan`, `Encounter`-linked notes, or extensions, and preserve provenance/linkage so the original aggregate assessment can be audited. Systems with generated R4 classes or REST endpoints must expect removed R6 resource-type support.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the core identity finding because the expected R6 StructureDefinition is absent, the R6 package index has no ClinicalImpression entry, and package-wide searches found no occurrence of the resource name. Confidence is medium for the replacement/mapping analysis because only local package artifacts were available; official ballot notes, JIRA, or migration ConceptMaps could identify recommended mappings not evident from the package.

This indicates removal rather than a local element-level remodel.

facts.note: No R6 StructureDefinition with this canonical URL was found in the package index.
Package-wide searches found no ClinicalImpression resource reference in the R6 package.
R6 ClinicalUseDefinition, Condition, DiagnosticReport, RiskAssessment, Observation, and CarePlan cover adjacent concepts but do not match the R4 resource identity or full aggregate assessment model.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old artifact was matched by exact canonical URL, id, type, and expected filename. No R6 artifact with that identity exists, and no close filename or index entry suggests a rename. Candidate related resources were identified only by clinical domain terms, not by structural or canonical continuity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and runtime break. An R4 instance with `resourceType: "ClinicalImpression"` can satisfy the R4 base resource definition, but a strict R6 validator or parser has no core resource definition to validate against. Generated R6 SDKs, JSON schemas, XML schemas, REST endpoints, and resource-type enums are also expected to omit this resource, so code that routes, stores, searches, or serializes by resource type will fail rather than merely warn.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The resource can contain clinically meaningful assessments, findings, investigations, and prognosis. Losing native support without a controlled migration can affect clinical context, auditability, and downstream decision-support workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Retire a low-maturity aggregate assessment resource and rely on more specific clinical resources or implementation-specific profiles.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain ClinicalImpression in base R6 as a deprecated or retired resource while directing new implementations to more specific resources.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Retiring an R4 trial-use/FMM 0 aggregate assessment resource is a plausible R6 goal, and a clean removal would reduce long-term base-spec and implementation burden. The local evidence, however, shows only absence from the R6 package and no official rationale or sanctioned successor. Because a base R6 design could have retained the resource as deprecated or retired and avoided the hard `resourceType` break, the level of breakage is not clearly justified on the supplied evidence. The alternative is only partial because it would undermine cleanup by preserving a legacy resource that implementations might keep using indefinitely.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base design would keep `ClinicalImpression`'s canonical StructureDefinition and R4-compatible content model in R6, mark it deprecated or retired, and add conformance guidance that new workflows should use more specific resources. That would preserve most R4-valid instances and generated APIs. It is not merely migration tooling, but it has material costs: R6 would continue to carry and test a low-maturity aggregate resource, servers could expose both legacy `ClinicalImpression` and newer decomposed representations for the same clinical facts, and the deprecated path might never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 wire compatibility, but keeps a low-maturity aggregate resource in core and creates an indefinite legacy representation alongside preferred R6 patterns.

examples.examplesMd: The example is intentionally minimal: it contains the R4-required local `status` and `subject` elements. Under the supplied R6 core package, the failure occurs before child-element validation because `ClinicalImpression` is not a recognized resource type.

findings.narrativeMd: `ClinicalImpression` moved from being a concrete R4 resource to having no native R6 core artifact in the supplied ballot package. This affects every R4 system that stores, exchanges, validates, or generates code for the resource. The break is not limited to one optional field: the whole resource type and all of its local elements disappear from the R6 core model.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `ClinicalImpression` instance can become R6-invalid because the R6 validator has no StructureDefinition for the resource type. Strict parsers and generated R6 libraries are likely to reject the `resourceType`, omit the class, and omit REST/search affordances. The R6-to-R4 direction is not applicable for native `ClinicalImpression` instances because none can exist as conformant R6 core resources.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all R4 `ClinicalImpression` usage before upgrading. Decide whether to preserve records as legacy R4 payloads, transform them into a bundle of R6 resources, or carry original details through extensions/profiles. Test validation, persistence, search, subscriptions, analytics, and generated-code paths that assume a `ClinicalImpression` resource type. Do not use a blind field rename; no direct R6 target was found.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Complete removal is the most disruptive option. A backward-compatible transition could have kept the resource with deprecated status, made profiles or best-practice guidance point elsewhere, and supplied a ConceptMap for element-level migration. That alternative would reduce validation and runtime breaks but would keep an arguably obsolete aggregate resource in the core surface.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official R6 ballot narrative, change proposals, or work-group notes before finalizing a production migration policy. The local package evidence is strong for absence, but it does not reveal the intended replacement strategy.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 has `ClinicalImpression` as a concrete resource, while the supplied R6 ballot package has no matching StructureDefinition, package-index entry, or package-wide reference. That means an R4 `resourceType: "ClinicalImpression"` instance, generated model class, REST endpoint, or search surface will not carry forward as a native R6 base resource. This is a real whole-resource compatibility break, but I would not mark it `Revisit` on the current evidence: the R4 artifact is FMM 0/trial-use, quick public-documentation checks show generic SDK support but not broad production IG use, and retaining the resource in base R6 would keep a low-maturity aggregate assessment model alive indefinitely.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-ClinicalImpression.json: id/type ClinicalImpression, kind resource, abstract false, status draft, standards-status trial-use, FMM 0.
R6 package check: StructureDefinition-ClinicalImpression.json is absent; .index.json has no ClinicalImpression filename/id/url/type entry; package-wide search found no ClinicalImpression references.
R4 package index contains ClinicalImpression search parameters; the R6 package index contains none.

Lightweight web check: HAPI/Firely/Python SDKs expose R4 ClinicalImpression for spec completeness, but I found no strong evidence of broad production use or inclusion in major production IGs such as US Core.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0 and trial-use substantially soften the stability concern. The removal is technically hard-breaking, but low maturity means the base specification has more room to retire the resource unless there is strong implementation or safety evidence; the quick check did not find broad production-use evidence.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: an R4-valid ClinicalImpression resource has no R6 base StructureDefinition, generated class, resource-type enum entry, REST endpoint, or search parameters in the supplied package.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design exists in the narrow sense: R6 could retain ClinicalImpression as deprecated or retired while directing new implementations to more specific resources. That would preserve most R4 wire/API compatibility, but it is not low-cost because it would keep a low-FMM aggregate resource, duplicate newer representations, and impose ongoing validator/search/codegen support.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing impact and alternative judgment. I agree the resource removal is a hard compatibility break and that retaining a deprecated resource is only a partial alternative, but the existing Critical framing overstates the action concern once FMM 0 and the lack of broad production-use evidence are applied.

findings.title: No single R6 resource preserves ClinicalImpression's aggregate assessment shape

oldState.summary: R4 ClinicalImpression is an aggregate clinical-assessment container.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 resource can combine business identifiers, status, subject, encounter, assessment time, assessor, previous assessment, problems, grouped investigations, summary text, findings, prognosis, supporting information, and notes in one resource.

newState.summary: R6 retains adjacent resources but no direct aggregate replacement was identified.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Condition`, `Observation`, `DiagnosticReport`, `RiskAssessment`, `CarePlan`, and `ClinicalUseDefinition` cover overlapping clinical concepts, but their root definitions show narrower or different purposes. None is an exact renamed `ClinicalImpression` or a single resource with the same aggregate assessment content model.

facts.note: Candidates are semantically adjacent but not a direct structural successor.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The candidate resources were identified by clinical domain overlap and root descriptions, not by exact canonical continuity. This supports a migration-risk finding, not a claim that the standard formally split ClinicalImpression into these resources.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Once the native resource is removed, implementers must choose a decomposition strategy. R4-to-R6 transforms can lose the fact that a clinician made one coherent assessment unless an explicit container, provenance, or extension strategy is added. Conversely, R6 data represented across separate resources will not automatically round-trip back to a single R4 `ClinicalImpression` with the original grouping, ordering, status semantics, and narrative context.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The clinical risk depends on local use. If systems used ClinicalImpression as the main container for diagnostic reasoning or assessment summaries, lossy decomposition could hide context that clinicians or quality workflows rely on.

justification.inferredGoal: Move assessment content to more specific resources rather than preserve a broad aggregate container.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: A base R6 transitional aggregate resource, or retained deprecated ClinicalImpression, could preserve grouping while steering new content to specific resources.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The likely goal of avoiding a broad aggregate assessment container and using more specific clinical resources is reasonable. A ConceptMap, StructureMap, profile, or extension strategy would be important migration mitigation, but it is not by itself a backward-compatible base R6 design. The actual base-design alternatives all keep or recreate an aggregate container, which would reduce migration loss but materially conflict with the goal and create two same-domain representations. For that reason, the absence of a single aggregate R6 successor is probably justified, while still requiring careful migration guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base alternative would be to retain `ClinicalImpression` as a deprecated transitional resource, or add a first-class R6 transition container that preserves the original assessment identity, status, time, problems, investigations, findings, prognosis, and notes while linking to preferred resources. This would cover common R4 records better than pure decomposition. Its tradeoff is substantial: R6 implementers would need to support both the aggregate and decomposed forms, mappings could be ambiguous when both are present, and old aggregate representations could accumulate indefinitely. Standalone cross-version maps, profiles, or extensions are useful mitigations but should not be counted as a `Yes` base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Material duplicate-representation and interoperability costs: the same assessment facts could be carried both in an aggregate container and in specific R6 resources, with ambiguous validation, search, and indefinite legacy support.

evidence.detail: R4 local elements include assessment status, subject, encounter, effective time, previous assessment, problems, investigations, findings, prognosis, supporting information, and notes.
R6 Condition is about conditions, problems, diagnoses, or clinical concepts that have risen to concern; it is not an aggregate assessment container.
evidence.quote: Detailed information about conditions, problems or diagnoses

evidence.detail: R6 DiagnosticReport covers diagnostic-test findings and interpretation, not the full ClinicalImpression content model.
evidence.quote: A Diagnostic report - a combination of request information, atomic results, images, interpretation, as well as formatted reports

evidence.detail: R6 RiskAssessment covers likely outcomes and likelihoods, corresponding to only the prognosis/risk part of ClinicalImpression.
evidence.quote: Potential outcomes for a subject with likelihood

evidence.detail: R6 ClinicalUseDefinition concerns indications, contraindications, interactions, undesirable effects, or warnings for products, devices, or procedures; it is not a patient-specific clinical impression.
evidence.quote: A single issue - either an indication, contraindication, interaction or an undesirable effect for a medicinal product, medication, device or procedure

examples.examplesMd: A typical R4 `ClinicalImpression` with `problem`, `investigation.item`, `finding.itemCodeableConcept`, `prognosisReference`, and `summary` may need to become multiple R6 resources plus linking metadata. Without a profile-specific rule, a later R6-to-R4 transform cannot know which findings and investigations belonged to the same original assessment.

findings.narrativeMd: The absence of a direct successor creates a conversion problem beyond resource-type validation. `ClinicalImpression` is an aggregate record of an assessment; the obvious R6 resources each capture only pieces of that record. Implementers must decide what the assessment itself means in their workflow and how to preserve that identity when content is distributed across other resources.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This finding is not a separate old-valid/new-invalid rule beyond the resource removal. Its compatibility effect is round-trip and runtime: transforms can produce individually valid R6 resources while losing the single-assessment grouping that an R4 consumer would need to reconstruct a `ClinicalImpression`. Strict code generation can also lose the original class boundary and search/index model.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a migration profile before converting data. At minimum, preserve the original `ClinicalImpression.identifier`, `status`, `subject`, `encounter`, `effective[x]`, `date`, `assessor`, and `previous` relationship, and explicitly link generated R6 resources back to the source assessment using `Provenance`, extensions, identifiers, or a local container pattern. Test round-trip cases with multiple findings, multiple investigation groups, prognosis codes/references, and entered-in-error status.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A formally published mapping artifact would be a less disruptive alternative to leaving each implementation to infer a decomposition. It could still encourage use of specific resources while preserving enough metadata to reconstruct R4 `ClinicalImpression` for cross-version exchange.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding intentionally does not assert that R6 officially split ClinicalImpression into the listed candidate resources. It reports the practical migration risk observed from the local package: no single native replacement is evident.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The mapping problem is real but derivative of the resource removal: R4 ClinicalImpression can carry one assessment identity with status, subject, encounter, timing, previous assessment, problems, investigation groups, findings, prognosis, supporting information, and notes. The adjacent R6 resources I checked cover narrower pieces rather than a single renamed successor, so an implementation that used ClinicalImpression would need a profile-specific decomposition and could lose the original assessment grouping without extra linkage. Still, for base R6 this appears proportionate: the artifact was FMM 0/trial-use, public evidence for broad production exchange is weak, and preserving a generic aggregate container would materially conflict with the likely cleanup goal.
keyEvidence: R4 ClinicalImpression local elements include required status and subject plus identifier, encounter, effective[x], assessor, previous, problem, investigation, finding, prognosisCodeableConcept, prognosisReference, supportingInfo, and note.

R6 Condition, Observation, DiagnosticReport, RiskAssessment, CarePlan, and ClinicalUseDefinition root definitions cover adjacent clinical concepts but not the same single aggregate assessment container.
No R6 ClinicalImpression StructureDefinition or direct successor was found in the package index or package-wide search.
Lightweight web check found SDK availability but no strong evidence that ClinicalImpression is broadly profiled or mandated in major production implementation guides.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The low FMM reduces the burden on R6 to preserve a lossless base mapping for every R4 use. I still treat the migration as meaningful for actual adopters because decomposition can be expert-dependent and clinically contextual, but low maturity and limited public adoption evidence keep it below `Revisit`.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss and runtime/API/codegen: individually valid R6 Condition/Observation/DiagnosticReport/RiskAssessment resources do not by themselves identify the original ClinicalImpression grouping, ordering, status, and narrative context; generated code also loses the old aggregate class boundary.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A transitional aggregate resource or retained deprecated ClinicalImpression would be less lossy for existing data, but it would create duplicate base representations and ambiguous precedence when the same facts appear both in the aggregate and in specific resources. ConceptMaps, StructureMaps, extensions, or local profiles are useful migration mitigations, but they are not themselves less-breaking base R6 designs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing impact and alternative judgment. I agree there is high migration and round-trip risk for systems that actually used ClinicalImpression, and I agree the available base-design alternative is only partial; I would soften the broad impact concern because the artifact is FMM 0 and quick usage checks did not show widespread production dependence.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: No ClinicalImpression-specific local invariant change was identified separately from removal. R4 snapshot constraints visible on root and backbone children are inherited `dom-*`, `ele-1`, and `ext-1` style constraints, which are out of scope for this resource report.
The R4 ClinicalImpression snapshot does not define local slicing on its own elements. No R6 counterpart exists where local slicing could be compared.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value on R4 ClinicalImpression was identified as a separate migration issue. The resource-level removal subsumes element availability.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraint on R4 ClinicalImpression was identified as a separate issue.

No matched R6 elements exist for a per-element cardinality comparison. The material cardinality effect is the root artifact removal captured in the identity finding rather than a child element min/max change.

No direct R6 successor elements were found for choice-type or datatype comparison. R4 `effective[x]` allowed `dateTime` and `Period`; R4 finding/prognosis choices and references have no native R6 ClinicalImpression element to compare.

R4 reference targets were checked for `subject`, `encounter`, `assessor`, `previous`, `problem`, `investigation.item`, `finding.itemReference`, `prognosisReference`, and `supportingInfo`. No direct R6 ClinicalImpression target set exists; no additional local reference-target narrowing was found beyond resource removal.

R4 local bindings include required `ClinicalImpression.status` and example bindings for status reason, code, investigation sets, condition code, and prognosis. Because the R6 resource is absent, there is no direct binding-strength or value-set comparison; terminology expansion was not needed to establish the main break.

R4 `ClinicalImpression.status` is a local modifier because `entered-in-error` changes interpretation. No R6 ClinicalImpression status element exists, so there is no separate modifier-flag flip; the semantic risk is included in the resource-removal and conversion findings. Inherited modifier-extension behavior is out of scope.

R4 summary flags on local elements such as identifier, status, code, description, subject, encounter, effective[x], date, assessor, and problem were reviewed. No R6 ClinicalImpression summary surface exists for comparison.
